---
title: "Photography"
lightbox: true
---

Ever since I became open-water certified in February 2018 in Hawai'i, I've been fascinated with scuba diving and underwater photography. I started with a GoPro 4 and now use a GoPro HERO 7.

[<i class="bi bi-camera"></i> More photos on Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/ademerlis/){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

::: {.panel-tabset .column-page}

## Corals Close-Up

I took these photos using a dissecting microscope, either through the eyepiece or with an image-capturing program. Most of the corals pictured are juveniles (less than 1 year old). Photos taken at Mote Marine Laboratory and in the Cnidimmunity Lab at the University of Miami. Click a photo to see the species name. [Learn about coral anatomy](https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/education/tutorial_corals/coral01_intro.html).

::: {.photo-grid}

## Fluorescence

Corals have a natural fluorescence that can be seen using blue light and a yellow filter, and different species fluoresce differently. All of these corals are juveniles (less than 1 year old). Some of these photos were featured in a [Nightsea article](https://www.nightsea.com/articles/coral-restoration-mote-marine-laboratory/) about the coral restoration work at Mote Marine Laboratory.

## Bonaire

I traveled to Bonaire in August 2019 to volunteer with [Reef Renewal Foundation Bonaire](https://reefrenewalbonaire.org/), a non-profit coral reef restoration group. Bonaire is a scuba diver's paradise: you can shore-dive to some of the most amazing, healthy, fishy reefs I've ever seen.

## Florida Keys

The Florida Keys have some fun dive sites, and I've been lucky to visit a lot of them, from my internships at Mote Marine Laboratory and the Reef Environmental Education Foundation (REEF) to fun dives.

::: {.photo-grid}
